## TL;DR

Task #1050 carries the E2 and E3 changes, and E1 is satisfied by `main`. The branch tip `7de76e042` is a merge of `main`; `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD main` against today's `main` returns one clean tree id with no conflict section, so the review's merge-conflict finding is resolved rather than pending. The other review finding — a running-checks capture showing the wrong state — was a shot-plan bug: `drawer:statusChecksRunning` seeds fixture task `9999`, but the plan pointed at real task `1050`, so no fixture state could render. The plan now uses `/work?task=9999` and highlights `.drawer-quickbar`; it also includes the established `repo:dirtyMain` panel shot for E2. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on this tip (format, lint, build, CSS/contrast guards, and UI smoke; the test step was delegated to the remote validation runner). I ran the four affected test files locally: 90 tests passed.

## Work and rationale

### E1 · No Restart work button while checks run

E1 overlapped with #1054, which landed on `main` first. Rather than keep two implementations of the same gate, the merge accepted main's version: `TaskCard.vue` is byte-identical to `main`, and both the card's `action` computed and its "running checks" hint read `showCardCheckProgress`, which is `activeTaskChecksBusy(repo, id, now)`. In the drawer, the Start/Restart, Review, and Pause buttons all gate on the same helper through `activeChecksBusy`. Because one helper feeds the status and the hidden buttons, the two cannot disagree — including after a reload or for a CLI-requested handoff. No branch-only E1 code or test remains; main's `active-task-card.test.ts` and `task-drawer-status-summary.test.ts` cover the acceptance criteria.

### E2 · Close the Uncommitted changes panel after a successful commit

`RepoDirtyPanel.vue` refreshes repository status after a successful commit and then sets `open.value = false`. It closes even when other files are still dirty, which the task explicitly allowed: the success toast already reports the file count, branch, and sha, and a panel stuck on "Uncommitted changes · Working tree is clean." with a stale success note was the reported oddity. The previously added `committedNote` is gone, so there is no redundant in-panel text. Failures still leave the panel open with the error and verbatim hook output. `repo-dirty-panel.test.ts` asserts the panel unmounts on success, remains open on a 409 and a 422 with hook output, and never shows the stale clean state.

### E3 · Collapse repeated agent stderr lines

`chat-rows.ts` now collapses only adjacent identical stderr lines into one row, carrying `repeatCount`, `firstAt`, and `at`; the original entries stay attached so expansion and export keep every line. A different line, a new timestamped record, or any intervening event breaks the run. `ChatDiagnosticRow.vue` renders a neutral `agent-diagnostic-neutral` entry labelled "Agent output" with an `×N` count and first/last times, and shows the full text on expand. Real turn failures keep their existing error surface; this component no longer paints ordinary CLI stderr red. `chat-tool-rows.test.ts` covers a 21-line run, run boundaries, multiline detail preservation, the collapsed patch summary, and the absence of error styling.

The branch-specific files are `ChatDiagnosticRow.vue`, `RepoDirtyPanel.vue`, `TaskDrawer.vue` (only the `detail-text`/`first-at`/`count` props at its two diagnostic render sites), `chat-rows.ts`, and the chat and dirty-panel tests.

## Approaches tried

The previous review reported merge conflicts in `TaskCard.vue` and `TaskDrawer.vue`. I confirmed the current state rather than repeating a merge: `git log` shows `7de76e042` as a merge of main at `05c7b6eba`, `grep` finds no conflict markers under `src`, and `git diff main...HEAD` is exactly the E2/E3 change set plus review reports. `TaskCard.vue` has no branch diff at all, and `TaskDrawer.vue` differs from main only by the E3 diagnostic props. To prove the finding is stale rather than merely resolved by luck, I ran `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only HEAD main` against today's main tip: it returned a single tree id and no conflict output, so a review preflight or close-out merge today is clean. I deliberately did not stage or commit a manual merge; the branch's existing merge commit already preserves both sides, and close-out merges from current main.

I also reworked the declared shots, which had been causing capture failures and the review's "wrong state" note. The old plan used `/work?task=1050`, but `drawer:statusChecksRunning` seeds fixture task `9999` through `SHOT_PREVIEW_FIXTURE_TASK_ID`, so the state could not render on a real task route — the capture fell back to the real drawer, which showed the task's actual status. The new plan is `/work?task=9999` highlighting `.drawer-quickbar`, where the handoff-in-flight fixture hides Restart work and the status line reads "running checks". For E2 I kept a known-good panel shot: `repo:dirtyMain` on `/`, click `[data-test-id="side-git-dirty"]`, highlight `[data-testid="repo-dirty-panel"]`. I did not add a shot for E3 because no preview fixture seeds agent stderr chat rows; inventing one would be new scope, and the component tests cover the collapse and neutral styling.

Verification this turn: `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed format, lint, build, CSS layering, theme contrast, hard-coded color, rendered contrast, bare-require, task-asset, and UI smoke. The gate delegated the test step to the remote validation runner. I separately ran `bun run test` on the four affected files (`chat-tool-rows`, `repo-dirty-panel`, `active-task-card`, `task-drawer-status-summary`): 90 tests passed.

## Challenges and blockers

The prior handoff failed at verify with "timed out waiting for the task's browser capture". A previous session also saw `repoos shot` time out reaching the server while `repoos stats` reported memory pressure and several WebKit processes. That reads as an environmental capture timeout, not a selector or route miss: the command never reached selector evaluation. I corrected the plan and did not retry in a loop or start my own server. If the handoff capture times out again, the remaining variable is preview reachability under memory pressure rather than the shot declaration.

No unresolved merge or worktree changes remain. The report is left as a local RepoOS draft for finalization against the checked tree.

## Key learnings

When a bundle item lands on `main` while its task is in review, drop the duplicate implementation rather than reconcile it: the merged branch is smaller and the shared helper guarantees card and drawer agree. A conflict finding is worth re-testing with `git merge-tree` against today's main before assuming the branch must change again. Shot fixtures that seed task `9999` must be shot on `task=9999`; a real task id silently renders the real drawer with no fixture state, which is exactly what the review captured. And a capture failure that says the server was unreachable is not evidence that the selector or route is wrong — distinguish the two before editing the plan.
